```{r}
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyverse)
STEERmon<- read_csv("data/STEER pilot Outplant Data - Monitoring Data.csv")

#selecting for columns that are in the primary datasheet, and organizing them so they are in the same order

#note Clump_ID=Tag ID, Health=Mortality 
STEERmon<-STEERmon%>%
  select(Monitored_By, Monitoring_Date, Outplant_Location, Clump_ID, Plant_Number, Mortality, Mainstem_Height, Tallest_Branch_Height, Number_of_Branches, Leaves_on_Mainstem, Leaves_on_Branches, `PropRoots?`, Notes)
```


```{r Dates}
#check the format of the monitoring date, and look and see if there is any months missing. If all the dates are in the same format you can use lubridate functions to tell R they are dates

unique(STEERmon$Monitoring_Date)
#double check date format
STEERmon$Monitoring_Date<-mdy(STEERmon$Monitoring_Date)

#if the dates arent all the same format, use parse_date_time(STEERmon$Monitoring_Date, orders = c("ymd", "dmy", "mdy")) using whatever orders are present in the vector


unique(STEERmon$Outplant_Location)
#looks good, only BC, bovoni cay


#want to see how many times all the clump IDs and plant numbers were monitored. Investigating any low numbers for potential typos
check<-STEERmon%>%
  group_by(Clump_ID, Plant_Number)%>%
  summarise(length(unique(Monitoring_Date)))

#these numbers have NAs in plant number gonna look into this and see why 630, 2229, 2396, 3123
check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==630)

check1<-check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==2229)

check1<-check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==2396)

check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==3123)
#they are dead, stopped numbering plant numbers after death


#this number only monitored once 
check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==2296)
#this is an error, likely a typo from 2396 fixed
STEERmon <- STEERmon %>% 
  mutate(Clump_ID = if_else(Clump_ID == 2296, 2396, Clump_ID))#if else statement, if clump ID is our problem child, replace with correct number, if not, keep clump ID


#3113 only has one monitoring data, something fishy here gonna check
check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==3112)
#only monitored 2/27/26, i think should be 3113 going to check to see if this one is missing this date
check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==3113)#double checked this was outplanted 2/23, 

#3122 and 3123 both were monitored in FEB, so this is 3113, will change
STEERmon <- STEERmon %>% 
  mutate(Clump_ID = if_else(Clump_ID == 3112, 3113, Clump_ID))

#2217 only monitored once
check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==2217)

check2<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==2277)
#2277 is missing July this 2217 should be 2277

STEERmon <- STEERmon %>% 
  mutate(Clump_ID = if_else(Clump_ID == 2217, 2277, Clump_ID)) #fixed


#3296 only once
check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==3296)
#should it be 3796? 
check2<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==3796)#nope

check3<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Monitoring_Date=="2025-11-21")#whats missing from this date

check3<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Monitoring_Date=="2026-01-02")#or whats monitored here but not date before?
#it should be 2396
STEERmon <- STEERmon %>%

#might be some weirdness going on with 4377

STEERmon<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(!(Clump_ID==4377 & Plant_Number==7))

check3<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==4377)

  group_by(Clump_ID)%>%

```

I feel like I should check that each clump id is only monitored once on each date
```{r}
#this tells me if when looking at each plant within each clump which plants were monitored more than once on a single monitoring date, I'll take a peek at these and see whats up, if it looks like the data was entered twice or if something is wonky

monCheck<-STEERmon%>%
  group_by(Clump_ID,Plant_Number, Monitoring_Date)%>%
  summarise(N=n())
#there are some that are monitored more than once, but these are NAs for the clumps that died, once they died people stopped tracking them 123

#however, clump 2229 on 2026-06-25 was monitored twice, gonna investogate

check<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==2229)
#one set was done by MN, one by GE, LA

unique(STEERmon$Monitoring_Date)
#looks like its missing data for 7/24 going to check who did monitoring on 7/24
#either data is entered twice or the wrong data is input and the duplicate is the july data

check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Monitoring_Date=="2026-07-24")
#all 7/24 was AB, gonna double check who all monitored in 6/25

check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Monitoring_Date=="2026-06-25")
#both GE, LA and MN did monitoring on this date. mystery solved. It was monitored by both groups on accident and entered twice gonna remove one of the duplicates

STEERmon<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(!(Clump_ID==2229 & Monitoring_Date=="2026-06-25" & Monitored_By=="MN"))

#check it worked
check1<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==2229 & Monitoring_Date=="2026-06-25")
#boom shaka laka!

#double check this
monCheck<-STEERmon%>%
  group_by(Clump_ID,Plant_Number, Monitoring_Date)%>%
  summarise(N=n())

```


```{r Categorical Variables}
#now going to start checking levels for factors
unique(STEERmon$Outplant_Location)
#looks good, only BC, bovoni cay

unique(STEERmon$Mortality)
#"A"  "D"  "DY" might want to change DY to A, for analysis, Not going to do that here tho

unique(STEERmon$`PropRoots?`)
#"N"  "Y"  "--" "-"  NA   "y" 
STEERmon<-STEERmon%>%
  mutate(`PropRoots?`=recode(`PropRoots?`, 
                             "y"="Y",
                             "--"="NA",
                             "-" ="NA"
                             ))
```

```{r Continuous Variables}


unique(STEERmon$Leaves_on_Branches)
#some dashes these will be forced to NA when made numeric
STEERmon$Leaves_on_Branches<-as.numeric(STEERmon$Leaves_on_Branches)
unique(STEERmon$Leaves_on_Branches)
#these look good, no clear typos
#looked at the range of the data by clicking on the top of the column in the dataframe, nothing out of normal ranges


unique(STEERmon$Leaves_on_Mainstem)
STEERmon$Leaves_on_Mainstem<-as.numeric(STEERmon$Leaves_on_Mainstem)
unique(STEERmon$Leaves_on_Mainstem)
#these look good, no clear typos
#looked at the range of the data by clicking on the top of the column in the dataframe, nothing out of normal ranges


unique(STEERmon$Number_of_Branches)
STEERmon$Number_of_Branches<-as.numeric(STEERmon$Number_of_Branches)

unique(STEERmon$Mainstem_Height)
STEERmon$Mainstem_Height<-as.numeric(STEERmon$Mainstem_Height)
#potential outlier clump ID 1501 has a recorded height of 435 and 1503 has one of 100 going to check these out and see whats up!

check<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==1501)#this should be 43.5

STEERmon<-STEERmon%>%
  mutate(Mainstem_Height = if_else(Mainstem_Height == 435, 43.5, Mainstem_Height))#fixed


check<-STEERmon%>%
  filter(Clump_ID==1503)
#im a little skeptical of this height, but i cannot rule it out for now, so the 100 stays until there is future height data to disprove it

unique(STEERmon$Tallest_Branch_Height)
STEERmon$Tallest_Branch_Height<-as.numeric(STEERmon$Tallest_Branch_Height)
unique(STEERmon$Tallest_Branch_Height)
#nothing looks out of the ordinary here!

```

```{r, Clean! Make CSV}

write.csv(file="STEERmonitoringCleaned11.26.csv", STEERmon)
```
